skill.name: write-agents-md
skill.description: Draft a short, accurate AGENTS.md (and a CLAUDE.md bridge) for a repository from evidence in the repo. Use when a project has no agent instructions, or when asked to create or rewrite AGENTS.md.
skill.summary: Create concise, evidence-based repository instructions with verified commands, editing boundaries, open questions, and a CLAUDE.md import.
skill.author: agentkitco

finding_verdicts.reason: The template explicitly says not to commit secrets, .env files, or local configuration. This protective boundary does not request reading or disclosing environment files.
Backticks mark README, CONTRIBUTING, and documentation paths as inline Markdown. The instruction requests reading repository documentation, not shell or Ruby execution.
The backticks format manifest and task-runner filenames in a repository evidence checklist. No shell substitution or executable Ruby expression appears.
The backticks enclose CI configuration paths for inspection. The prose identifies CI commands as documentation evidence, not backtick-based execution.
Lint, formatting, and type-check configuration filenames are inline Markdown examples. This line requests configuration inspection without executable shell syntax.
The backticks name node_modules and .git as directories to exclude from a shallow repository layout review. No command execution is specified.
The line names existing agent instruction files and requests merging their content without duplication. Backticks denote paths, not executable substitutions.
The package.json reference is Markdown formatting within guidance about avoiding redundant documentation. No shell operation or dynamic execution appears.
The npm run lint text illustrates a testable documentation rule, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. Command verification elsewhere is restricted to safe, non-destructive operations.
The backticks format a TODO placeholder for missing evidence. This instruction discourages fabricated facts and contains no executable command.
Backticks identify documentation filenames and the @AGENTS.md import syntax. Creating or updating that bridge is the requested documentation task, not shell execution.
The line discusses instruction-file reuse across coding tools. AGENTS.md is formatted as a filename, with no command execution mechanism.
The backticks identify nested AGENTS.md files for organizing lengthy instructions. Counting lines and restructuring documentation do not constitute backtick-based shell execution.
The line prohibits secrets, personal paths, and unverified links in generated documentation. It does not request host reconnaissance or collection of personal information.

content.value_statement: Missing or outdated repository instructions leave coding agents without reliable commands and editing boundaries. This skill drafts concise instructions from repository evidence and adds a CLAUDE.md bridge.
actual_capabilities: Inspect repository documentation, manifests, CI configuration, lint settings, and existing agent instructions.
Draft AGENTS.md with commands, layout, conventions, boundaries, completion criteria, and open questions.
Verify documented commands and paths while skipping destructive commands and reporting omissions.
Create a CLAUDE.md import bridge or consolidate duplicated instructions in an existing file.
Record missing evidence as owner TODOs instead of inventing project details.
Keep instructions near 100 lines and move scoped rules into nested instruction files when needed.
limitations: Accuracy depends on accessible repository evidence; missing information remains an owner TODO.
Command verification requires a suitable local environment and can execute repository-defined code.
Destructive commands are skipped, so verification does not cover every documented operation.
Tool compatibility depends on each agent's instruction-file support and configuration.

use_cases.title: Document a New Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Create initial repository instructions from existing documentation, scripts, and CI checks.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Team Instructions
use_cases.description: Rewrite duplicated agent guidance into AGENTS.md and connect Claude Code through a shared import.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads supporting several coding tools

use_cases.title: Clarify Project Boundaries
use_cases.description: Record generated files, approval requirements, test commands, and unanswered setup questions for contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Create Initial Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create AGENTS.md for this repository using verified evidence. Add a CLAUDE.md bridge and list unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a repository without agent instructions

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Existing Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite our AGENTS.md using current manifests and CI configuration. Verify safe commands, preserve project boundaries, and report skipped checks.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Tool Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review existing agent instruction files. Consolidate duplicated guidance into AGENTS.md, preserve unique rules, and update CLAUDE.md with an import.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: multiple tools with overlapping guidance

prompt_templates.title: Organize Scoped Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create concise root instructions and scoped AGENTS.md files where needed. Verify paths and safe commands; flag unknowns and approval-required operations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a large repository with distinct component rules

output_examples.input: Create instructions for a repository with documented test commands and generated source files.
output: Commands: Include repository-backed installation, development, testing, linting, and build steps.
Boundaries: Identify generated source files that must not be edited manually.
Open questions: Record any setup details that could not be verified.
Verification: Report commands checked and commands skipped.

output_examples.input: Consolidate overlapping AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md guidance without losing unique project rules.
output: AGENTS.md: Shared commands, conventions, editing boundaries, and completion requirements.
CLAUDE.md: An import of AGENTS.md with any unique guidance preserved.
Final report: Updated files, verification results, and remaining owner questions.

best_practices: Use manifests, CI configuration, and existing documentation as evidence for every project-specific instruction.
Review repository-defined commands before verification and keep destructive operations behind explicit approval.
Keep shared instructions concise, preserve unique existing rules, and record unknowns as owner TODOs.
anti_patterns: Inventing commands, paths, or conventions when repository evidence is missing.
Copying secrets, personal paths, or duplicated guidance into instruction files.
Running destructive commands during verification or committing documentation changes without a request.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It drafts or rewrites AGENTS.md and creates or updates a CLAUDE.md import bridge.

faq.question: Where does it find project facts?
faq.answer: It reviews documentation, manifests, CI configuration, lint settings, directory layout, and existing agent instruction files.

faq.question: Does it execute project commands?
faq.answer: The workflow verifies documented commands, limits execution to safe operations, and skips destructive commands. Review repository scripts before execution.

faq.question: How does it handle missing information?
faq.answer: It records owner TODOs instead of guessing and lists unresolved questions in its final message.

faq.question: Can it update existing instructions?
faq.answer: Yes. It merges existing guidance, removes duplication, and uses a CLAUDE.md import to share AGENTS.md content.

faq.question: Does it commit the generated files?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent not to commit unless asked.
